This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/settings-service.mdx`  _(via setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 123ff6f4e2faa4beffcf1875618c358bc1692c95` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `a986561e0ada5c3f89e1ecc8525b568536e8c7d2` — the merge of head `576b82834cd74ce0fc09692d4a58476d5ca822c5` into base `123ff6f4e2faa4beffcf1875618c358bc1692c95`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin a986561e0ada5c3f89e1ecc8525b568536e8c7d2 && git checkout a986561e0ada5c3f89e1ecc8525b568536e8c7d2

git fetch origin 123ff6f4e2faa4beffcf1875618c358bc1692c95 576b82834cd74ce0fc09692d4a58476d5ca822c5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 123ff6f4e2faa4beffcf1875618c358bc1692c95 && git merge --no-ff 576b82834cd74ce0fc09692d4a58476d5ca822c5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 123ff6f4e2faa4beffcf1875618c358bc1692c95
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 123ff6f4e2faa4beffcf1875618c358bc1692c95` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `576b82834cd74ce0fc09692d4a58476d5ca822c5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-getmany.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-organization-isolation.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-organization-reach.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-user-rung-owner.pin.test.ts + .changeset/25202-settings-no-organization-less-rung.md (judged under ②), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (`resolveGuestOrganization` :1274-1294 at the merge-base; `resolveLocalizationContext` :2407-2560), packages/core/src/security/system-write-organization.ts (`resolveSystemWriteOrganization`, the D9 predicate and its decision type), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`resolveSystemInsertOrganization` and `probeInstallOrganizations`, the write-side asker of the same predicate), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts (:1102 `branding.workspace_name`, :1155 `localization.locale`, :1800 `auth` global key, all read with an empty context), packages/cloud-connection/src/runtime-config-plugin.ts (:1172 anonymous `branding` `getMany` with an empty context), packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts (:882-903 `lifecycle.retention_overrides`, once with no organization and once per organization), packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts (:661-664 `sys_setting` fate `attribution`), packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-harness/fixture-18.0.0/database.sql (:665-666 the two `sys_setting` rows, :895 the identity index), docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md on `origin/main` (D1 :234-270 with the `6328195425` amendment, D8 :663-696 with the `6325596117` note, D9 :698-733 with the `6328987873` / #25133 letter-A note, D13 :870-889).

Inputs read: card #25202 body, its claim (`6339806560`) and the os-dev-report (`6342115583`); the parent's reconciliation note `6339761793` on #15212; the PR body and file list; `git diff 9c431bad371f62bf5edac369d2405745ee1155e7 576b82834cd74ce0fc09692d4a58476d5ca822c5` (9 files, +527/−118); the 47 check-runs on the head. The working checkout in this container is behind `origin/main`, so every cited file was read by ref (`9c431bad`, the head, or `origin/main`), never from the working tree.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The reach, before and after — which `sys_setting` rows a tenant- or user-rung read admits.** Before (merge-base `settings-service.ts` :150-170, :1822-1833, :2935-2940, :2984-2994): `own(X)` queried each rung crossed with `organization_id IN {X, NULL}` and `preferredRow` fell back to the NULL row; `organization-less` (no organization behind a wall) read the NULL rows alone; `unwalled` (no organization under `single` or no posture source) read every row and preferred the first organization-stamped one. After (head :150-184, :1853-1855, :1867-1878, :2976-2980, :3006-3041): `own(X)` reads `organization_id = X` and nothing else; `no-organization-object` reads `organization_id = NULL` alone; `unowned` loads no `sys_setting` row at all (`loadScopedRows` :3012 returns empty). The one predicate `withinReach` (:2976) now drives the engine `$or`, the in-memory filter (:2965-2971) and the rung's pick (:1853), so the three cannot disagree. **Right:** D1 as amended ("nothing reads a NULL tenant value as an owner") and D8 ("no layer has a NULL arm; no shared-owner set") are met for every reach that names an organization. A NULL-organization row is still admitted only through `no-organization-object`, reached (a) when the engine's predicate answers `no-organization-object` — the composition registers no `sys_organization`, exactly the #25133 letter-A case the D9 note keeps — or (b) when no organization source is bound at all (`organizationReachOf` :1872: `if (!source) return no-organization-object`). The in-repo production binder (the plugin, :344-345) always binds one; (b) is a host-binding residual, flagged in ③, not a reading any served composition reaches.

**2. A caller with no organization, by posture.** `organizationReachOf` (:1867) asks the wall first, then the source. Under `group` / `isolated`: `unowned` — no tenant or user rung; the global rung (`sys_platform_setting`, `loadGlobalRows` :2990, loaded by `loadRowSets` :2944 for every reach) and the default answer; a tenant-scope write is refused at the service (:2227, `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `constraint: { scope: 'tenant' }`). Under `single` with exactly one organization: `own(X)` where X is `resolveGuestOrganization(engine, posture)`'s `derived` answer — the same `resolveSystemWriteOrganization` the engine's insert path asks, over the same probe (`sys_organization`, `limit: 2`, system context: core :1286 and engine :7765), so the read side derives the organization the write side stamps. Under `single` with zero or several organizations: `refuse` → `unowned` (reads from the global rung or default; tenant write refused) — the engine already refused such writes (`no-organization`, `ambiguous-organization`), so the service now agrees with it rather than reading "whichever row came first". Lean embedding (no `sys_organization` registered): `no-organization-object` → NULL rows read and written, as ruled. No posture source, or one reporting none, reads as `single` (plugin :345 passes `undefined`, core :1283 defaults it) — the same "no posture is no wall" reading the authorization face gives. **Right, and the derived organization is D9's.**

**3. Legitimate callers.** plugin-auth's email brand name (:1102) reads `branding`, a namespace the plugin offers only where no wall stands (`UNWALLED_ONLY_NAMESPACES`, plugin :80), so it now reads the one organization's own row — the row it already preferred under `unwalled`. plugin-auth's auth locale (:1155) is a tenant key read under every posture: `single` → the derived organization's row; walled → global rung or default, where before it read NULL rows only — on a served walled store those exist only as ceremony-reported rows, so this is the declared narrowing and nothing else. The anonymous `runtime/config` branding read (:1172) is `single`-only by the manifest gate → derived. Lifecycle's organization-less `retention_overrides` read (:882-893) → derived under `single`, global/default under a wall; the per-organization loop (:894-903) names each organization and is unchanged. `resolveLocalizationContext` for a signed-in user with no active organization (:2471-2498, `{ tenantId: undefined, userId }`) → same pattern. The settings HTTP door (`verifiedContextFromRequest`, plugin :392-462) hands the vetted `tenantId` from `resolveRequestExecutionContext`; a caller with no active organization is the same case. `auth` and the other process-wide namespaces are `global` keys, read with `UNOWNED` (:1625, :1732) — the global rung is loaded regardless of reach and `scope === 'global'` is excluded from `loadScopedRows` in the query, so **no process-wide reader loses the global rung.** The 18.0.0 harness test (new, :406-420) pins both routes: `GET /api/settings/branding` as the admin and `settings.get(branding.workspace_name, {})` / `settings.get(localization.timezone, {})` answer `source: 'tenant'` from the fixture's two owned rows.

**4. The write side.** Head :2289: `organizationId = scope !== 'global' && reach.kind === 'own' ? reach.organizationId : null`, so the row's identity (`rowIdentity` :3129-3152) and `upsertRow`'s existence probe name the organization the reach owns. The reported defect is real on the merge-base: the service wrote `organization_id: null` under a system context, the engine's `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` stamped the derived organization on insert (rows lacking the tenant column are the ones it decides, engine :7839-7858), and the next probe for `(…, organization_id NULL)` missed that row and inserted beside it — on SQL the `COALESCE(organization_id,'__global__')` identity index (fixture :895) refuses the second insert instead. The fix is right and lands no write in a different organization than before: under `single` with one organization the engine was already stamping the derived organization; the service now names it up front. Walled, caller-named organizations are unchanged (`own(X)` always was X). A user-scope write by an `unowned` caller still passes `organization_id: null` and is refused by the engine (`ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`), as before — the PR body says so. `reset` (`resetNamespace` :2850) resolves through `getNamespace` and `setMany` with the same context, so it clears the derived organization's rows, consistent with what it read. `audit.record` keeps `tenantId: ctx.tenantId` (undefined for a process-wide writer) — the ledger insert is itself a system write the engine derives under `single`, so the ledger row lands in the same organization; `auditWriter.organizationId` follows the reach (:2412). The lock pre-flight (:2232-2243) picks with the same `preferredRow`, so the row that answers a read is the row whose lock refuses the write; a lock on a NULL row locks no organization (pinned).

**5. Cross-organization leakage under a wall.** None: `own(X)` admits X alone; a caller naming none admits nothing; `setMany` under `own(X)` writes X's row and never finds another organization's (pinned: the organization's write lands beside the NULL row, `[[null,'Legacy'],[ORG_A,'Alpha']]`). The reach pins (`settings-organization-reach.pin.test.ts`) run the real `SettingsServicePlugin` on a real `ObjectKernel` with a real `ObjectQL` and its `tenancy` service, so the source under test is the one the plugin wires.

**6. R1–R4.** R1 (fresh store boots and serves), R2 (18.0 and 18.0.0 fixtures upgrade and keep their data, the 18.0.0 leg now including the settings-still-answer test) and R3 (the v17 trait is refused, takes the ceremony, boots) are the `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)` lane, **success** on this head (run started 14:34:44Z, completed 14:40:37Z; the earlier run was `skipped` before the seat's label). R4 (walled boot): the service's walled behaviour is pinned under `group` and `isolated` with the real engine and the real plugin; the dogfood shards (`Dogfood Regression Gate (shard/3)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`) are `skipped` on this head because `ci.yml` runs them only off `pull_request` events (:2037), so no walled app boot was measured pre-merge, locally or in CI — see ③.

**7. Tests edited beside the pins.** `settings-getmany.test.ts` and `settings-user-rung-owner.pin.test.ts` drop the contexts that named an organization against fixture rows carrying none — right under D8 (such a read no longer falls back), and the user-rung pin keeps its `{}` and `{ userId }` controls. `settings-routes.test.ts` renames the private-reach literal `unwalled` → `no-organization-object` for a service bound with no source — right. No reference to the retired kinds or `ANY_ORGANIZATION` remains anywhere at the head.

**8. `main` moved.** Nine commits since `9c431bad`; `git log 9c431bad..origin/main -- PATHS` over the PR's nine files is empty. One later commit, `3a440b01f6` (#25210), touches `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` and `tenancy/system-write-organization.ts`: the tenant-audit mute moves from the per-table ledger to the schema, and an explicit `bypassTenantAudit: true` (which `loadScopedRows` :3039 passes) stays honoured; `resolveSystemInsertOrganization`'s decision body is untouched. No effect on this diff.

**9. Gate verdicts on the head** (`/commits/576b8283…/check-runs`, 47 runs, latest run per name): 34 `success`, 8 `skipped` (Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Temporal Conformance — event- or path-filtered), **0 failures**. `Check Changeset` success twice (13:35:58Z and the label-triggered re-run 14:36:14Z); `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `check-governed-merges --branch`: 0 of 9 paths governed.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25202-settings-no-organization-less-rung.md`: `'@objectstack/service-settings': patch`; summary `fix(service-settings)!: …`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; the `**BREAKING**` banner; FROM / TO and the remedy; the adr-0087 comment marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, bare and line-initial.

- **Level.** Under ruling A (2026-10-21, #25105 — `AGENTS.md` on `origin/main` :1082-1093; the `WHICH LEVEL` paragraph of the `Check Changeset` step, `pr-automation.yml` :754 ff.) the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". This diff changes which stored `sys_setting` row answers a read and gives `bindEngine` one optional input; no authorable key, value, type, default or meaning changes, so `none` is the right kind and `patch` is the right level. The level axis in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (`judgeLevel`) requires a declared `none` to grade every introduced entry `patch` — satisfied — and the `Check Changeset` lane that runs it (and the `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` step at :999 of the same job) is green twice on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.** The claim expected `no (narrowing)`; the dev re-declared from the diff. `yes` is earned: `SettingsService.bindEngine`'s `extras` accept a new optional `organization` input (a widening of a published class's accept set; `export type SettingsOrganizationSource` is module-level and not re-exported from `index.ts`). `(narrowing)` is the face: a tenant- or user-scope `sys_setting` row with a NULL `organization_id` stops answering any organization's read, and a `single` caller naming none now reads nothing where D9 derives no organization. Under ruling A the `yes` no longer forces `minor`, so the declaration and the level agree.
- **ADR-0087 marker.** `no-migration-prescription` is honest: the body prescribes no consumer code rewrite — the remedy is an operator data action (`os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN`, re-save each reported value inside its organization, or declare the key `global`), nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite, no tombstone, no export removed. Mechanically, the detector finds no `OPERAND → OPERAND` rewrite and no `FROM … → … TO` label line in it (the `Setup → the settings page` fragment has no operand on either side), and the gate passed. The marker's "other categories closed on facts" paragraph is accurate.
- **Who is affected / remedy** are stated and match the measurement: fresh installs and `os serve`-written 18.0.0 stores hold no such row (fixture :665-666: both rows owned by `org_mvgqf77lj6oc60fk`); a v17 store under `single` has them attributed by the ceremony (inventory :661-664, fate `attribution`, D10 fate 3); walled stores keep them NULL and reported, and from this release those rows answer nobody.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev flag — `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally** (shallow clone, partial build). Answered: every lint, type-check and build lane on this head is `success`, and those two checks run there; nothing is owed.
2. **Dev flag — walled dogfood boot NOT MEASURED locally; "CI's dogfood lane covers it".** Not on a PR: `ci.yml` :2037 runs the dogfood shards only when `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, so they are `skipped` on this head and R4 rests pre-merge on the walled pins (service + real engine + real plugin on a real kernel). Escalated to the seat as a residual, not a block: the first post-merge `main` battery is the compensating measurement of a walled boot, and the plugin's wiring (:337-345) is posture-independent, so the pins exercise the same seam the boot would.
3. **`open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`** — two findings the dev did not list, both outside this PR's surface, for cards under #15212's gate ③:
   - **a.** `resolveLocalizationContextUncached`'s direct fallback (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` :2537-2545 at the merge-base) reads `sys_setting` with `scope: 'tenant'` and **no organization filter**, taking the first row per key — an any-organization reading outside the settings service, with NULL rows admitted. It is reached when the settings service is absent or throws; after this PR an organization source that throws (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError` from `tryFind`, not caught by `organizationReachOf` by design) is one more way to reach it. Pre-existing; not this diff's.
   - **b.** `SettingsService.bindEngine` without an `organization` source reads as the lean composition (NULL rows) on any composition (head :1872). The in-repo production binder always wires it, but `index.ts` documents hosts that bind their own engine ("control-plane mocks, embedded runtimes"); such a host on a composition that registers `sys_organization` keeps a NULL arm and the very duplicate-insert shape this PR fixes. Suggest the service derive from the bound engine when the source is unset, or refuse. Not blocking: no served composition in this repo reaches it.
4. **Observation, no action owed:** `resolveGuestOrganization` is asked once per no-organization read of a non-global key (and once per `setMany` batch); core's copy carries no memo where the engine's probe does (engine :7754). A `sys_organization` probe per such read is a cost, not a correctness question; `resolveLocalizationContext` keeps its own cache in front of it.
5. **`needs:upgrade-harness`:** the dev judged the ceremony inventory unchanged and the label not owed; the seat applied it anyway and the lane ran green on this head. No contradiction, and the lane's result is what certifies R1–R3 here.
6. **`Clause-②` re-declaration** from the claim's `no (narrowing)` to `yes (narrowing)` is accepted (② above); the claim said the dev measures first and re-declares from the diff, and the diff carries the widening it names.

## Seat check

- **Shape:** 9 files, +527 / −118. `check-governed-merges --pr 25226`: 0 of 9 paths governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing.
- **What it does:**
  - The settings service's tenant and user rungs stop admitting an organization-less `sys_setting` row (ADR-0131 D8; D1 as amended). `own(X)` reads X alone. A caller with no organization reads the organization D9 derives under `single`, and nothing under a wall. Only the ruled lean-embedding composition still reads NULL rows (#25133, letter A).
  - The global rung is read as before.
  - It also fixes a live defect: under `single`, a no-organization caller saving a key twice inserted a second row, losing the write. On SQL the identity index refused it.
- **Review:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, narrowing face, from an isolated reviewer: **PASS** 6343868210 at this head.
  - The reach is right for every kind.
  - The derived organization is the one the engine's insert path stamps.
  - No legitimate caller loses the global rung, and nothing leaks across a wall.
  - The changeset is right: `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (a widening `bindEngine` input beside the narrowing), `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING, and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- **CI:** the latest run of every check is success or skipped. The opt-in `18.x upgrade harness` lane, which the seat labelled, passed on this head; it covers R1–R3, including the PR's new 18.0.0 "settings still answer" test.
- **R4, measured before landing.** `ci.yml` skips the dogfood shards on `pull_request` and `merge_group`, so the seat asked the dev for a walled boot. On this head, a production `os serve` of the showcase was run under `isolated` and under `group`, with a secret, an owner email, invite-only membership and `@objectstack/organizations` composed through a temporary local rig that was restored afterwards.
  - Both reached "Server is ready", and health answered 200.
  - A signed-in user with no active organization read settings 200, all defaults.
  - After creating and activating an organization, a settings write and re-read answered from the tenant rung.
  - The boot log has 0 ERROR lines, and every `sys_setting` row carries an organization.
  - Source: the dev session's own measurement on `576b8283`. Its message to the seat is pending the session owner's approval, and the seat read the results from the session record.
- **Carried from the review's ③, filed as cards by the seat:**
  - `resolveLocalizationContextUncached`'s direct `sys_setting` fallback in core reads with no organization filter;
  - a host that binds `SettingsService` without an organization source reads as lean (NULL rows).
- **Landing:** the seat flips the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `Fixes #25202` closes the card.
